Let me parse this certificate.

Certificate:
- number: R51/1996-NL1-05.02 revision 1 → number: "R51/1996-NL1-05.02", revision: "1". Scheme: A (conformity certificate, first-type evaluation? OIML-CS scheme A is for certificates issued on basis of type evaluation reports... Actually OIML Certificates of Conformity are scheme A; scheme B is MAA. This is NMi issuing an OIML Certificate of Conformity — scheme A.)
- project_number: 510417
- page_total: 2
- member_state: The Netherlands
- date_issued: 19 January 2006 → "2006-01-19"
- oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly. Omit.

- address_lines: ["Hugo de Grootplein 1", "3314 EG Dordrecht", "The Netherlands"]

certified_type:
- category: "Automatic catchweighing instrument"
- type_designations: family: DACS-W-***-**, DACS-W-***-**N, BC-W-***-**, BC-W-***-**N, DACS-H-***-**, DACS-H-***-**N
- description: none beyond family

model_family:
- family_name: null (the "Family of type" is a list of designations)
- models: the family covers 6 designations. But attributes don't vary per model — the class/Max range applies to the family. Hmm. Should I create models for each designation? The attributes given (330 g ≤ Max ≤ 5500 g etc.) are type-level, not per model. The schema says model_family include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Here it covers 6 type designations. I think listing models with model_id as each designation is reasonable. But attributes vary only by ranges. Alternatively skip model_family since there is no per-model attribute matrix. Hmm.

The rule: "model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". The cert covers 6 designations (a family). I'll include model_family with models[] each model_id being a designation. Characteristics stay type_level since they apply to whole family.

characteristics.type_level:
- accuracy_class: X(1) → value "X(1)" string. Or "X". The certificate says "Class X(1)" and "for accuracy class X(1)". Canonical: accuracy_class: {value: "X(1)"}. Also recommendation.accuracy_classes: ["X(1)"].
- maximum_capacity: {min: 330, max: 5500}, unit g
- minimum_capacity: {min: 15, max: null}, unit g
- verification_scale_interval_e: {min: 0.2, max: null}, unit g — label: "minimum_verification_scale_interval"? The text says "e ≥ 0.2 g". Canonical label: "scale_interval" or "verification_scale_interval". I'll use "verification_scale_interval".
- number_of_verification_scale_intervals: {max: 3300} → n ≤ 3300 → {min: null, max: 3300}, dimensionless.
- maximum_belt_speed: 60 m/min → value 60, unit "m/min"
- temperature_range: {min: -5, max: 40}, unit °C

recommendation:
- id: "R51"
- edition: 1996
- amendment: null (omit)
- scheme: "A"
- accuracy_classes: ["X(1)"]

test_reports:

- R51/1996-NL-97.02B, 41 pages
- R51/1996-NL-97.02C, 32 pages
- R51/1996-NL1-05.02, 38 pages

Also "type-approval certificate and the description with number T2869" — could be a documentation_file? It says "represented by the sample or samples identified in the associated Test Report, the type-approval certificate and the description with number T2869 and the appertaining documentation folder". T2869 is a description/type-approval certificate number. Add test_reports entry: id "T2869", role "documentation_file". Hmm, it's a description. I'll include it as documentation_file.

footnotes: none defined.

Type designations with asterisks: "DACS-W-***-**", etc. In JSON strings fine.

Model family: include models list of the 6 designations. Each model_id: "DACS-W-***-**" etc. Label maybe same. I'll include.
